The output includes an interactive map with dynamically updated layers based on user selection and classification visualization of agricultural and natural land covers within HCPs.
rows.task_head: Task: Monitor HCP vegetation and cropland

rows.task_full:
Task: Analyze monthly maximum kNDVI
Compute a time series of monthly maximum kNDVI (kernel NDVI) from MODIS MOD13Q1 data between 2005 and 2020, applies a tanh-transformed NDVI scaling, and visualizes both the individual monthly composites and their long-term mean over a user-defined region. It also generates a chart of the monthly maximum NDVI time series and clips outputs to the input geometry.
rows.task_head: Task: Analyze monthly maximum kNDVI

rows.task_full:
Task: Analyze NDVI in study area
Analyze vegetation health in a specific administrative district (Amphoe) in Thailand using Sentinel-2 satellite imagery from August 2021. It computes the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) by applying the formula (NIR - Red) / (NIR + Red) using bands B8 and B4, clips the result to the study area derived from FAO GAUL level2 boundaries, and visualizes it with a color palette. Additionally, it generates a time series chart of mean surface reflectance values for selected bands over the region and displays a false-color composite image (B8, B4, B3) masked by cloud cover less than 10%. Outputs include the NDVI layer, a border overlay of the administrative unit, and a chart showing temporal reflectance trends.
rows.task_head: Task: Analyze NDVI in study area

rows.task_full:
Task: Detect deforestation using Sentinel-1 VH backscatter change
Detect tropical or temperate forest loss between 2015 and 2024 using dual-polarization (VV/VH) Sentinel-1 GRD SAR imagery. It computes a pre-deforestation VH reference (2015), a post-deforestation VH image (2024), applies two thresholds — forest presence (VH > −12 dB in 2015) and significant decline (ΔVH > 3 dB) — to generate a binary deforestation mask, calculates the total deforested area in hectares within the ROI, and visualizes the change via RGB composites and comparative VH histograms. Outputs include interactive map layers (VV/VH, ratio, change composite, deforestation mask), a quantitative area statistic (hectares), and a bivariate histogram comparing 2015 vs. 2024 VH backscatter distributions.
rows.task_head: Task: Detect deforestation using Sentinel-1 VH backscatter change

rows.task_full:
Task: Analyze Kabul City LST trends
Analyze land surface temperature (LST) patterns in Kabul City using MODIS MOD11A2 data from 2000 to 2019. It processes both daytime and nighttime LST bands by scaling pixel values (multiplying by 0.02) and converting from Kelvin to Celsius. The workflow includes filtering the image collection by region and time, computing mean temperatures over the study area, and generating a time series chart comparing day and night LST. Two charts are created: one for general comparison and another focused on regional mean LST trends by label. Outputs include printed image collections and a time-series chart of surface temperature variation over two decades.
rows.task_head: Task: Analyze Kabul City LST trends

rows.task_full:
Task: Classify land cover using optical and radar data
Classify land cover in the Niayes region using a combination of Landsat 8 surface reflectance, Sentinel-1 SAR, and derived spectral indices (NDVI, NDWI). It applies cloud masking to Landsat and Sentinel-2-like QA60-based masking (though not used), computes NDVI and NDWI, fuses optical, radar, and index bands, and performs Random Forest classification using training samples. Three classifications are generated: (1) using only Landsat spectral bands and indices, (2) using fused Landsat and Sentinel-1 VV/VH bands, and (3) using all bands including indices. Each classification is validated using an error matrix and overall accuracy is reported. Outputs include classified raster maps and accuracy assessment results.
rows.task_head: Task: Classify land cover using optical and radar data

rows.task_full:
Task: Extract NDVI time series for sites
Extract NDVI time series from Sentinel-2 TOA reflectance imagery over specific field sites (DPM) using cloud-masked data. It applies a custom cloud masking algorithm (S2CloudRemvAlg1), computes NDVI using bands B8 and B4, and generates a line chart of NDVI values over time for each site. Additionally, it labels the sites on the map and exports per-image NDVI values at specific locations via reduceRegions. Outputs include a labeled map of sites, an interactive NDVI time series line chart, and feature collection of NDVI values extracted at site locations for further analysis.
rows.task_head: Task: Extract NDVI time series for sites

rows.task_full:
Task: Extract precipitation data
Extract monthly TRMM precipitation data from the 'precipitation' band within a specified date range and geographic region, clips it to the region of interest, and exports each image in the collection to Google Drive.
rows.task_head: Task: Extract precipitation data

rows.task_full:
Task: Identify least cloudy Landsat image
Identify the least cloudy Landsat 8 image from a specific WRS path and row by sorting the image collection based on the 'LAND_COVER' metadata property and selecting the first (least cloudy) image. It visualizes this image in true color and generates a time series chart of mean spectral values within a 500-meter buffer around a sample point, using a 30-meter scale. Outputs include the selected image, a true-color visualization, a sample point overlay, and a chart of spectral reflectance over time.
rows.task_head: Task: Identify least cloudy Landsat image

rows.task_full:
Task: Analyze B4 vs B6/B5 ratio
Generate a scatter plot of Landsat 8 TOA band 4 (red) values against the ratio of bands 6 and 5 (SWIR1 and NIR) for pixels within San Francisco, visualizing spectral relationships in the urban landscape.
rows.task_head: Task: Analyze B4 vs B6/B5 ratio

rows.task_full:
Task: Classify land cover types
Classify land cover into four classes—water, urban, and two vegetation types—using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data and a Random Forest classifier trained on user-defined feature collections. The output is a classified raster map with distinct color-coded land cover categories and an accuracy assessment via confusion matrix.
rows.task_head: Task: Classify land cover types

rows.task_full:
Task: View near real-time flood and crop conditions
the workflow provides an interactive tool for visual inspection of near real-time satellite imagery to support flood response and crop monitoring. It enables users to draw an area of interest, filter images by date range, and overlay multiple satellite datasets (Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, Sentinel-3, Landsat-8, NAIP) with different visualizations (true/false color, SAR) to assess surface conditions.
rows.task_head: Task: View near real-time flood and crop conditions

rows.task_full:
Task: Extract and visualize S2 NDVI images
Process Sentinel-2 imagery from April 2020 to compute and export NDVI visualizations for multiple dates, focusing on cloud-masked, surface-reflectance images clipped to a specific region. The outputs are false-color NDVI images exported to Google Drive.
rows.task_head: Task: Extract and visualize S2 NDVI images

rows.task_full:
Task: Analyze NDVI and EVI time series
Analyze temporal patterns of NDVI and EVI vegetation indices over a user-defined region using MODIS MOD13A1 data from 2017 to 2022. It generates a time-series chart of mean index values, creates animated thumbnails with date overlays for NDVI and EVI separately, and exports a CSV table of the monthly reduced values. The workflow includes image collection filtering, scaling of pixel values, region-based reduction, visualization with custom palettes, and interactive UI updates based on user-drawn geometries.
rows.task_head: Task: Analyze NDVI and EVI time series

rows.task_full:
Task: Compute NDVI from Landsat bands
Calculate NDVI using near-infrared (B8) and red (B4) bands from surface-reflectance-corrected Landsat 8 TOA imagery collected between July 15 and October 15, 2021, over a user-defined region. It first composites the image collection by computing the mean, clips it to the study area, then computes NDVI as (NIR - Red) / (NIR + Red). The output includes a true-color RGB visualization layer and a false-color NDVI map with a divergent color palette ranging from red to blue via green, highlighting vegetation density variations.
rows.task_head: Task: Compute NDVI from Landsat bands

rows.task_full:
Task: Analyze vegetation and land cover temporal patterns
Analyze temporal patterns of multiple vegetation and land surface indices (NDVI, LSWI, EVI, NBR, etc.) and spectral bands across different land cover types (cropland, forest, tea plantations, etc.) in Xishuangbanna, Yunnan, using Landsat 8 and Landsat 7 data from 2018 to 2020. It generates day-of-year composite charts for each index and band, aggregated by region, to compare seasonal dynamics across land cover classes.
rows.task_head: Task: Analyze vegetation and land cover temporal patterns

rows.task_full:
Task: Analyze LAI time series
Analyze the Leaf Area Index (LAI) over Singburi Province using MODIS MCD15A3H data from 2019 to 2022. It filters the LAI image collection by date and region, computes the mean LAI image clipped to the province boundary, visualizes it on the map with a custom color palette, and generates a time series chart of mean LAI values extracted from the region. The outputs include a mapped LAI layer and an interactive chart showing temporal variation in LAI.
rows.task_head: Task: Analyze LAI time series

rows.task_full:
Task: Identify land cover clusters
the workflow segments Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery over a user-defined region of interest (initially set to 'congzuo' in Guangxi) using the SNIC (Simple Non-Iterative Clustering) superpixel algorithm. It first applies cloud masking and scaling to the image collection, computes a median composite for 2019, then clips a precomputed UNVI index (Urban Normalized Vegetation Index) to the ROI. The SNIC algorithm generates homogeneous spectral-spatial clusters at 10m resolution, which are used as labels to compute mean UNVI values within each cluster. The final output is a reduced connected components image representing mean UNVI per cluster, exported at 10m resolution for further analysis.
rows.task_head: Task: Identify land cover clusters

rows.task_full:
Task: Model projected January temperatures
Analyze future daily maximum near-surface air temperature in the San Joaquin watershed using NASA NEX-DCP30 climate model ensemble data. It filters for January months and RCP scenarios (2.6 and 8.5), converts Kelvin to Celsius, labels bands by scenario, and generates a time-series line chart showing median values with interquartile ranges. Additionally, it visualizes the median temperature for a specific year (2050) using a styled raster map over the region of interest.
rows.task_head: Task: Model projected January temperatures

rows.task_full:
Task: Generate seasonal vegetation composite
Generate a multi-season composite image by computing median values of Landsat 8 TOA reflectance and multiple vegetation and moisture indices (NDVI, EVI, RVI, DVI, NDWI, NDBI, SAVI, NDGI) across four seasonal periods in 2019–2020. It masks cloud-contaminated pixels, applies terrain variables (elevation, slope, aspect) from SRTM, and composites seasonal medians into a final 4-season stacked image (winter, autumn, spring, summer) clipped to a study area, which is then exported to a GEE asset.
rows.task_head: Task: Generate seasonal vegetation composite

rows.task_full:
Task: Compute mean sea surface temperature
Calculate the mean sea surface temperature (SST) during the Northeast Monsoon period from December 2019 to February 2020 by processing MODIS-Aqua L3SMI data, filtering for the specified time range, reducing the image collection to a single mean composite, and exporting the result.
rows.task_head: Task: Compute mean sea surface temperature

rows.task_full:
Task: Analyze NDVI time series
Analyze the MODIS NDVI time series at a specific point of interest in California, applies cloud masking using the SummaryQA band, and generates a scatter chart of NDVI values over time. It further performs temporal smoothing by joining each image with its neighbors within a 17-day window and computing the mean NDVI across the matched images, then visualizes both raw and smoothed NDVI time series.
rows.task_head: Task: Analyze NDVI time series

rows.task_full:
Task: Analyze NDVI time series
Analyze the temporal dynamics of NDVI in Rwanda using Landsat 8 surface reflectance data from 2010 to 2020. It filters the NDVI image collection by date and spatial bounds, rescales pixel values by applying a multiplicative factor (0.0001) through a mapping function, and generates three time-series charts: a mean NDVI profile over Rwanda, a day-of-year composite series, and a year-stratified day-of-year NDVI trend. The outputs are interactive charts visualizing seasonal and interannual vegetation patterns.

Task: Classify land cover using multisensor fusion
the workflow prepares a multi-source remote sensing data stack combining Sentinel-2 optical bands, Sentinel-1 SAR (VV and VH), terrain attributes (slope, aspect, TWI), and vegetation/water indices (NDVI, NDWI) for supervised classification. It samples training data from user-defined geometries and existing samples, merges them, and exports the combined feature collection to a GEE asset for subsequent classification modeling. The output is a labeled training dataset suitable for land cover classification.

Task: Classify vegetation and agriculture areas
Compute NDVI from Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data for the year 2018, clips it to a user-defined geometry, and performs land cover classification using a Random Forest classifier trained on user-provided sample regions (Mata and Agricultura). The output is a classified image distinguishing between two classes—likely forest and agricultural areas—based on NDVI values, which is then exported to Google Drive.

Task: Extract NDVI from Landsat imagery
Process Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery over a user-defined region (pp) to compute and visualize median summer-fall (2017) true-color composites, and attempts to calculate maximum NDVI from winter-spring (2017) imagery. However, due to a bug (using 'ndvi.max()' instead of 'ndvi1.max()'), the NDVI output is incorrect. It clips results to the study area and adds both the composite and flawed NDVI layer to the map for visualization.

Task: Map surface temperature in Vienna
Compute and visualizes the mean land surface temperature (LST) in degrees Celsius for Vienna, Austria, using Landsat 8 Collection 2 Level 2 thermal band ST_B10. It applies cloud masking via QA_PIXEL bits, scales the raw ST_B10 values to Kelvin (using scale factor 0.00341802 and offset 149.0), converts to Celsius, clips the result to Vienna’s subdistricts geometry, and displays it as a single-layer raster map with a yellow-inclusive palette (min=28°C, max=47°C) on the GEE Code Editor map interface.

Task: Map annual fire occurrence
Map the spatial extent of thermal anomalies (fire detections) across Australia from 2000 to 2020 using MODIS Terra FIRMS data. It filters the FIRMS ImageCollection by the Australian polygon, aggregates detections per year by computing the maximum brightness temperature (T21) and applying a >100 K threshold to generate binary fire presence layers, then computes annual counts per region (AUS) to produce a time-series chart showing the total number of fire pixels detected each year. The output is a UI chart visualizing annual fire pixel counts (not burned area or fire events) and optionally a clipped binary fire layer for mapping.

Task: Classify land cover in river basin
Classify land cover types in the Rio do Coco basin using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery from April to May 2020. It applies cloud masking using QA60 bits for cirrus and cumulus clouds, computes NDWI and NDVI indices, and trains a Random Forest classifier on manually labeled training samples (water, exposed soil, pasture, forest). The classification uses B4, B3, B2, NDWI, and NDVI as predictors. The output includes a classified land cover map, accuracy assessment via confusion matrix on a test set (30% of samples), and export of the classified image to Google Drive.
rows.task_head: Task: Classify land cover in river basin

Task: Analyze NDVI variation over time
Analyze the temporal variation of NDVI in a defined region using Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data from 2017 to 2019. It computes NDVI by applying normalized difference on bands B5 and B4, maps the index over time, and generates a time-series chart of mean NDVI values within the study area. The output is an interactive chart displayed on the map showing monthly-annual trends, with no raster export or classification performed.

Task: Analyze seasonal VV and VH backscatter changes
Compute mean VV and VH polarized radar backscatter from Sentinel-1 GRD data across three seasonal periods (prior autumn, summer, and subsequent autumn), composites them into RGB false-color images to visualize temporal changes, and displays the clipped results over a geometry. The output highlights areas with changing backscatter characteristics over time, likely related to land cover dynamics such as vegetation growth or soil moisture variation.

Task: Analyze ETa over water balance area
Analyze actual evapotranspiration (ETa) within a defined water balance area using EEFLUX data from 2010 to 2015, generating time series charts of mean ETa with and without zero-value masking. It also visualizes the spatial extent of the water balance area and associated CIMIS stations, and prints summary statistics for a specific agricultural region (Calipatria).

Task: Extract NDBI from Landsat imagery
Calculate and exports the Normalized Difference Built-up Index (NDBI) from Landsat 8 Surface Reflectance data over a defined geographic region for the months of May to September between 2013 and 2020. NDBI is computed using SWIR (B6) and NIR (B5) bands, masked for clouds and cloud shadows, reduced in resolution via mean aggregation, reprojected to MODIS projection, and exported to Google Drive annually by date.
